title: Chronic kidney disease: stage, hypertension and dialysis status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic kidney disease and blood pressure management.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of chronic kidney disease. He reports feeling generally well today but notes occasional fatigue. He has been adherent to his prescribed medication regimen. He denies any recent acute changes in urinary output, significant edema, or new-onset symptoms. His blood pressure has been stable at home.

Medication List
Lisinopril 20mg daily, Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Vital signs show a blood pressure of 134/82 mmHg. Physical exam reveals no significant peripheral edema. Heart sounds are regular. Lungs are clear to auscultation. No acute distress noted.

Assessment
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 3b.
2. Hypertension.

Plan
Continue current medications as prescribed. The patient will continue to monitor his blood pressure at home and keep a log for the next visit. Follow up in three months for laboratory work and renal function monitoring.
explanations: Hypertension with CKD is presumed linked: I12.9 for CKD stage 1-4 (sequenced first), plus the N18 stage code.
CKD stage 3b: N18.32 (maps to a higher V28 HCC than 3a).

distractors.why: The classification presumes a link between hypertension and CKD.
I12.0 is for stage 5 or ESRD only.
3a is less severe than the documented 3b.
Stage 3b is documented; do not use unspecified stage 3.
